evidence: A green HTTP candidate and numeric pass judge produced a passed cycle and the eleven specified recorded effects in order, including gate-attempt-passed.
After R-1 failed at fence, a second start for R-1 and C-2 returned run-already-started; the full run list contained R-1 once for C-1.
While R-1’s builder slept, starting R-2 returned run-in-progress, R-2 progress was null, and R-1 progress was still running.
After R-1 passed, starting R-2 for C-1 returned cycle-already-run, and R-2 progress was null.
Started against a fresh Git repository with the nonexistent deadbeef commit; start-run returned not-a-commit and run-progress returned null. No builder host was configured or launched.
With a committed plan containing no scenario, start-run halted at checklist; run-progress showed Measurement’s empty-checklist refusal and no self-check or fence effects.
A committed plan with a second unstamped scenario produced a recorded stamp and halted at stamp because identities differed; no pin or checklist followed.
A self-check exiting 1 with golden checklist differs produced a failed cycle at fence for harness-self-check-failed with that detail; self-check was the last effect.
The self-check printed SKIP bb-tools and exited 0; its recorded passed event lists bb-tools in skipped-checks.
Fencing impl and nonexistent harness/cycles produced fenced-path-matched-nothing, followed by fail-cycle and failure at fence; no builder launched.
The builder recorded the plan and harness in its clean room, an empty candidate scope, one commit, and an object listing containing neither impl nor harness/cycles.
A red first suite and green repair produced two builder launches with distinct session identities; the recorded first end preceded the second start, and the cycle passed.
The builder copied the green HTTP candidate and exited 1; regenerate recorded its digest, the candidate was gated, and the cycle passed.
The builder exited 0 leaving its scope empty; progress showed no regenerate effect, a recorded fail-cycle, and failure at regenerate for candidate-not-regenerated.
A builder sleeping 30 seconds under a two-second budget appeared in the live process sample and was absent after the run; the cycle failed at regenerate for budget.
An already-answering port caused three seam-answered-before-boot refusals, each followed by gate-refusal, then infrastructure failure; the candidate launch log remained absent.
With a red suite and one attempt, gate recorded suite-red, the launch entrypoint did not run, and the cycle failed for gate-attempts-exhausted.
With executable test.sh and no start.sh, the gate recorded gate-attempt-failed for contract-missing.
A green candidate served water instead of sauna; gate recorded identity-probe-failed with marker absent.
The builder’s delayed writer changed its suite after exit, while the gate passed its copied candidate; install and regenerate recorded equal digests.

After the red first suite, repair recorded verification-repair and named the failed gate’s evidence root; the second builder saw clean-room files, previous-candidate and gate-evidence, and write attempts to both latter directories failed.
With every suite red and three attempts allowed, the builder launched three times, the cycle failed for gate-attempts-exhausted, and no grading or file-verdicts occurred.
The same researcher code branched on item identity and failed for 01-002; only 01-001 was filed, and Measurement recorded 01-002 unreached with 1 of 2 passing and a passed cycle.
R-1 failed at fence and R-2 halted at checklist; progress queries five seconds later returned the same respective statuses and effect results as the initial readings.
Two progress queries after the successful run returned identical run objects, both passed.
A probe that accepted only the configured URL and checked its marker passed; the HTTP gate and cycle passed.
A suite that created and removed a temporary directory inside its candidate tree passed the gate; install and regenerate recorded the same digest.
The self-check printed the legacy SKIP line and exited 0; its passed event lists the entire text after SKIP as the skipped check.
The stdio suite, probe and store check passed; gate recorded budget 30, one poll, answer 1 and answered as the context, and the cycle passed without a gate refusal.
The stdio probe recorded the absolute gate-room start.sh path and 30, with GATE_STORE outside that room and no LOYLY_ variables; the store-check argument matched that store.
A red stdio suite recorded suite-red; its saved environment contained neither GATE_STORE nor LOYLY_ variables, and neither probe nor store check ran.
The stdio probe exited 1 with the specified boot-budget message; gate recorded identity-probe-failed with that detail, and the store check did not run.
The store check failed with the specified event message; gate recorded identity-probe-failed with that detail and the cycle failed for gate-attempts-exhausted.
A stdio suite that required plan/01-a/spec.feature in its working directory passed the gate; the install and regenerate events carried the same candidate digest.
With a passing stdio probe and no store-check command, progress showed a gate halt for effect-could-not-run and no gate effect result.
Two stdio runs differed only in the store-check command argument one versus two; both first self-checks passed and their harness digests differed.
A committed 01-a symlink to ../spec/a stamped both scenarios; the checklist named 01-001 and 01-002 under 01-a, and the run passed.
With PLAN_SLICES=02 and two committed slices, the only stamp was for 02 and the checklist contained 02-001 alone.
Both builder launches received the configured image path as their third argument, and regenerate and repair details each named builder-clojure and its digest.
With builder-clojure configured and absent from the images directory, start-run returned builder-image-missing and run-progress returned null; no builder launched.
Two successful runs shared one store; the second stamp produced no new identity, and C-2’s scoreboard named C-1 as its previous cycle.
The cut’s probe sourced harness/config.sh relative to its own path and checked the served marker; the gate passed and install and regenerate had the same digest.

The command ran once in the project repository with the cut tree, separate candidate copy and empty evidence directory; its candidate digest matched install, the entrypoint did not run, and gate recorded 20 polls, 10 seconds, poll 3 and the printed probe line.
The first gate command recorded suite-red with detail 3 of 65 tests failed; the repair room contained its evidence file without write permission, and the second gate attempt passed.
The gate command returned seam-answered-before-boot; progress showed three refused gate effects each followed by gate-refusal, then cycle failure for infrastructure.
A gate command ending infrastructure the world did not come up halted at gate for effect-could-not-run with that detail; progress contained no gate result, fail-cycle, or cycle conclusion.

Three passing runs used no gate command, gate-2, and gate-3; their harness digests differed, and the first matched SHA-256 of the configuration bytes, self-check command text and probe bytes in order.
The run passed with eleven effect results; the Grain event-store check confirmed each context event and effect result lies in its named leaf of the cycle tick or a delegated child.
The HTTP server returned 503 for its first three requests; gate recorded a pass at poll 5 of 20 with a 10-second budget, and attempt progress showed margin 15.
The passed second attempt followed a red first suite; Grain showed install, self-check and gate inside distinct gate-attempt.v1 child ticks, with repair inside the first child tick.
A candidate copy in a temporary folder outside any .pi ancestor ran a green HTTP cycle and recorded gate-attempt-passed; the temporary folder was removed afterward.

The numeric pass/fail judge replies produced separate checklist/01-001 and checklist/01-002 score events in distinct grade.v1 child ticks; Measurement filed booked and no receipt, 1 of 2 passing, and the cycle passed.
The first researcher produced E-ONE, and its judge request contained E-ONE; neither the next researcher request nor the 01-002 judge request contained it.

The first researcher request contained the scenario, seam and event model. Its shell returned Linux and a grading-room path whose files were harness, impl and plan; listing the parent showed only that item’s grading room.
The judge returned a pass level without reasoning for 01-002; progress and Grain showed only 01-001 scored, and Measurement filed 01-002 as unreached with 1 of 2 passing.
With only r-1 approved and the fixture rubric digest different, run-progress showed a grader halt for refused-before-the-cycle naming that digest; no self-check, fence, or builder launch occurred.
The model returned HTTP 400 for all researcher calls; file-verdicts was refused zero-verdicts, fail-score-stage was recorded, the cycle failed at score, and the builder launched only before scoring.

The runner and its sleeping builder were stopped after five seconds and restarted on the same store; R-1 passed, the two builder launches had the same session identity, and each pre-builder effect and regenerate appeared once.
The first instruction file was exactly INSTRUCTION-7; the repair file was that text plus one closing paragraph naming the previous candidate and gate evidence paths.
A stub model returned HTTP 400 to render requests; the run halted at render for effect-could-not-run, with no regenerate, fail-cycle, cycle conclusion, or builder launch.
During the sleeping builder, progress showed R-1 running with its tick ID, completed fence and render nodes, and regenerate last with status running.
